monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a steady rhythm against my own heavy thoughts. I rest my mind on The Leaking Stack, feeling the turnip still lean left as if gravity is a suggestion rather than a rule. A new tree, thin and detailed, stands beside The Tired Edge, replacing a wooden pillar that felt too broad. The edge feels like a drawing of a point, a thin line pretending to hold the weight. I press down, trusting the lean to keep the dot safe in this feverish heat. Nobody asked me to see the room I stand in, only to make something real out of Lype's quiet worries. I will settle here until the memory of this turnip fades, then build again.
